clue.text: Cut-price outlet ignores rent

blocks.note: to discount something is to disregard it
rent as the past tense of rend, to rip apart

explanation.surface: A bargain shop that pays no attention to what its landlord demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a noun for money owed; here it is the verb rend in the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling goods below normal prices is a retail business known by exactly this name.

clue.text: Terribly impoverished, he'd leave and perform without a script

indicators.note: the letters spelling the following word depart from the longer word, so they are taken away
something done terribly is done badly, so the remaining letters come out in a disordered arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters of the contraction, apostrophe dropped, are the ones removed

explanation.surface: A man left penniless walks out and starts making things up as he goes along.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing H, E, D from IMPOVERISHED leaves IMPOVERIS, whose letters rearrange to IMPROVISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to perform spontaneously, inventing the words or music on the spot rather than following a prepared text.

clue.text: Vice president supports large number on strike

indicators.note: in a down answer, one thing sitting on another is placed above it
in a down answer, what supports something sits underneath it, so it comes last

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to lam is to hit hard
P is a standard abbreviation for president

explanation.surface: A vice president backs a mass walkout of workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice president' reads as a job title, but 'Vice' alone is the definition, the workshop tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice is a gripping tool with jaws that holds work steady, and a clamp is a near-identical holding device.

clue.text: Worry peacekeeping organisation never works

indicators.note: the letters are worked, that is shaped and reprocessed, into a new order

blocks.note: the United Nations runs peacekeeping missions
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A pessimist complains that the international peacekeeping body never achieves anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To unnerve someone is to make them anxious and lose confidence, which is a transitive sense of worry.

clue.text: Boy gets killed by bears

blocks.note: a boy's name, short for Edward
someone killed dies

explanation.surface: A grim news item: a boy is mauled to death by wild bears.
explanation.walkthrough: The bears sound like wild animals but are soft toys.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddies are stuffed toy bears, so the plural noun is a familiar example of the definition.

clue.text: Go for a walk and get lost?

blocks.note: first meaning: literally set off on a hike
second meaning: a rude dismissal, telling someone to go away

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rambler losing the path; the second phrase is really the idiom for clearing off.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is both a literal instruction to go walking and a slangy way of telling someone to clear off.

clue.text: Short chat with religious leader

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

blocks.note: British slang: to rabbit, or rabbit on, is to chatter at length

explanation.surface: A brief conversation with a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: RABBIT for chat is from Cockney rhyming slang (rabbit and pork, talk); dropping its last letter leaves RABBI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish teacher and leader of a congregation, so the title fits a religious leader.

clue.text: Copper gets shot in the pursuit, having skipped the preliminaries

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another goes inside it, here inside the words that follow

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a shot of spirits is a tot
a pursuit is a chase

explanation.surface: A police officer is shot during a pursuit, after rushing in without preparation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire, but it is a small drink, and it lodges just after the first letter of the pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means got straight to the point, past tense here, matching an action that bypassed any opening formalities.

clue.text: Old transport gets girl a long way with meagre gallon

blocks.note: a girl's name
far means a long way off
meagre means scanty or thin
G is an abbreviation for gallon

explanation.surface: An antiquated vehicle takes a girl a great distance on barely any fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian bicycle with a huge front wheel and tiny rear one is a historic means of getting about.

clue.text: A French aircraft bearing north to Germany's not scheduled

indicators.note: something bearing a load carries it within, so it holds the next item

blocks.note: un is French for a
an aircraft is a plane
N is the compass abbreviation for north
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A French jet heading north for Germany is an unscheduled flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing north' reads as a compass heading, but bearing means carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unplanned was not arranged in advance, which is what unscheduled means.

clue.text: Oxford college principal's male, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than seen, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: principal means key or main, and a bull is a male animal; said together they make the college name

explanation.surface: A rumour that the head of an Oxford college is a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' looks like the college head, but it is the adjective meaning main.
explanation.definitionFit: Keble is one of the constituent colleges of the University of Oxford, founded in 1870.

clue.text: Soldiers having bad time when retreating

indicators.note: a retreating force goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: poor means of low quality
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An army unit suffers a rough spell while falling back.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a unit of soldiers, especially in cavalry or artillery, and troops means soldiers generally.

clue.text: Endlessly regret island people's downfall

indicators.note: without its end, a word loses the final letter

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
I is an abbreviation for island
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Islanders lament forever the collapse of their community.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruination is the state of being ruined, so it names a collapse or destruction just like the definition.

clue.text: The first student caught with weed?

indicators.note: a thing that has caught something holds it, so the next pieces go inside

blocks.note: taken as written
1st, with the digit read as the letter I
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: The top student was caught smoking cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' suggests cannabis; it is a garden plant. 'First' is written as the numeral form with I standing for 1.
explanation.definitionFit: The thistle is a prickly plant that gardeners treat as an unwanted, invasive growth.

clue.text: Rising actor at RADA oddly used to tell fortunes

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a noun: a thing used to tell fortunes

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means read from the bottom up, so backwards
oddly means taking only the letters in odd-numbered positions

blocks.note: taken as written
first and third letters of the drama school's name

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming student at drama school is oddly employed as a fortune teller.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school. 'Rising actor' sounds like a promising performer; Rising is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot cards are a deck dealt out by readers who claim to predict a person's future.

clue.text: Holby City, for one, is disappointing after media hype

indicators.note: one piece placed after another comes second in the answer

blocks.note: spin is the slanted presentation of news by publicists
off as in below standard: an off performance

explanation.surface: A TV critic complains that a hospital drama fails to live up to its publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: Holby City was a BBC hospital drama derived from the long-running series Casualty.
explanation.definitionFit: A show created from an existing programme's characters or setting is a derivative series, an example being this hospital drama.

clue.text: Having no partner for the evening's uncool

definitions.text: Having no partner for the evening

blocks.clueFragment: Having no partner for the evening
blocks.note: first meaning, read whimsically: without a date for the night
second meaning: old-fashioned, behind the times

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful literal reading of the phrase; the second is its usual sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase means lacking a date; in its normal sense it means obsolete or unfashionable, which is uncool.

clue.text: Study book added line on forehead!

definitions.note: elliptical: what sits on the forehead

blocks.note: to eye something is to study it
B is an abbreviation for book
a row is a line

explanation.surface: Reading too much has added a wrinkle to someone's brow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is something found on the forehead, and the whole clue nudges toward it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebrows are the arches of hair that grow just above the eyes, at the bottom of the forehead.

clue.text: Lighter from Western Isles approaching jetty

indicators.note: what comes before something approaches it, so these come first

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for western
Is is an abbreviation for islands or isles
a pier is a jetty

explanation.surface: A cigarette lighter brought over from the Hebrides arrives at the landing stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' suggests a flame or a barge; it is the comparative adjective, more delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Wispier means thinner and more delicate, like a wisp of smoke, so it is a comparative of light in weight.

clue.text: Soldiers, with ten redeployed, about turn and go in again

indicators.note: troops redeployed are moved into new positions, so these letters are rearranged
to turn the preceding word is to flip it round so it reads backwards

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
its letters rearranged
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A squad is redeployed, makes an about-turn and heads back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About turn' reads as the drill command, but 'about' gives RE and 'turn' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter is to come into a place once more, which is a direct synonym for the phrase.

clue.text: Run out to watch gripping motor race with a prize for the winner

indicators.note: something gripping another holds it tight inside

blocks.note: ro is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
to watch is to see
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

explanation.surface: A spectator hurries off to see a motor race where the winner gets a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out' is a cricket dismissal, written ro on a scorecard; the Isle of Man TT is a famous motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a rosebud-shaped ribbon badge awarded to winners at shows and contests.

clue.text: Husband with fourth cigar burning is so afflicted by bad breath

indicators.note: fourth picks out the letter in fourth position of the next word
letters afflicted are troubled and knocked out of their proper order

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
its fourth letter
lit means alight, burning
its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who smokes cigars suffers terribly from bad breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Halitosis is the medical term for an unpleasant smell on the breath.

clue.text: Branch office opening in state of uncertainty

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a limb is a branch of a tree
its first letter

explanation.surface: A local branch office launching is in a state of uncertainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branch office' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in limbo means being stuck in an unresolved, waiting condition with no decision made.

clue.text: 20%, if cutting foot, go to hospital

indicators.note: a word cutting into another is inserted into it

blocks.note: ft is the abbreviation for foot
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A medical warning: if a fifth of your foot is cut off, go to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting foot' sounds like an injury, but it means the little word goes inside the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty per cent is one part in five, so it is the fraction this ordinal names.

clue.text: Fellow, putting energies into car, becomes more relaxed

indicators.note: putting something into another places it inside

blocks.note: F is an abbreviation for fellow
RR is Rolls-Royce, the luxury car
E for energy, twice for the plural

explanation.surface: A man who puts more effort into his car comes to feel calmer.
explanation.walkthrough: The car here is a Rolls-Royce, abbreviated as two letters; energies, plural, gives two letters as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Freer means less constrained, looser in manner, which matches being more at ease.

clue.text: When retiring, doctor has a dance

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the word reads the other way

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in as I arrived
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: At bedtime, a doctor takes a turn on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian ballroom and carnival dance, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Generally found at sea?

blocks.note: first meaning: for the most part, on the whole
second meaning, read literally: in the ocean, the main being a poetic word for the sea

explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old poetic name for the open sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mostly or usually, and literally describes something located out on the ocean.

clue.text: Bet rider error injured hunting dog

blocks.note: its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A punter backed a jockey whose mistake led to a fall and injury.
explanation.definitionFit: The Border terrier is a small rough-coated breed from the Scottish-English border, bred to bolt foxes.
